title: Cross-scope isolation under load (port isolation_load)
summary: Port the leakage assertions from benchmarks/isolation_load/run.py into a Locust User at 100 tenants x 1,000 agents x 200 users — the SDK's core differentiator and, per the strategy doc, its most important benchmark gate.
description:
Port the cross-scope-leakage assertion pattern from the existing `benchmarks/isolation_load/run.py` (10 tenants x 20 workers today) into a Locust `User` built on BM-12's harness: every returned row's scope must equal the requesting scope, scaled to 100 tenants x 1,000 agents x 200 concurrent users. Add a shared-`MemoryStore`-instance scenario specifically to exercise E3 (thread-safety of a single `MemoryStore` under concurrent use), which the capability inventory marks only "implicit" in the current isolation_load module, not explicitly tested.

**Coordinate with EPIC-12's BRUN-4 before deleting the old module.** BRUN-4 is the first-ever execution of `--suite isolation` and may still be "To Do" when this story starts. Check its status on the board: if BRUN-4 hasn't run yet, either let it run against the existing `isolation_load/run.py` first, or re-scope it to exercise this new Locust-based test instead and note the substitution in BENCHMARKS.md — either way, do not delete the module and leave BRUN-4 with nothing to execute against. Acceptance: leak count is 0 at full scale; a deliberately injected scope bug (e.g. temporarily dropping one scope predicate) is caught by the assertion, proving the gate actually fires; the run exits non-zero on any leak; `benchmarks/isolation_load/` is removed only after the coordination above is resolved. Depends on BM-12.
